purpose: F24 of the third independent review: the published second fix drops every request behind the FIRST one of a connection without answering it and without slowing or destroying the socket, so a flood pipelined behind a PENDING first request (a valid cancel waiting for its step boundary) is retained at about 1.8 KB per request until a small-heap server hangs or aborts (exit 134). The in-process tests count the requests behind the first one (at most 8 are tolerated, the ninth destroys the connection) and the process test attacks a 48 MB-heap child with 4 connections of 50,000 requests each; they run against the published server.cjs of the second fix (evidence/red/prefix-8832dac5) and must fail.
